problem_markdown: A simple polygonal path with distinct endpoints lies inside a square of side 100. Every boundary point of the square is within $1/2$ of the path. Prove that two path points at Euclidean distance at most one are separated along the path by length at least 198.
solutions_markdown:
Parametrise the path in traversal order. Let $A$ be the first square corner whose closed radius-$1/2$ disk the path reaches. Of its neighbouring corners, label the one reached first $B$ and the other $D$. Let $Z$ be the first path point within $1/2$ of $B$, and split the path at $Z$ into an initial and a final part.

On side $AD$, choose the last point $U$ toward $D$ that is within $1/2$ of the initial part. It exists because this covered set is compact and contains $A$; it is not $D$. Every point just beyond $U$ is therefore covered by the final part. Compactness of that part implies that $U$ also lies within $1/2$ of it.

Choose $X$ on the initial part and $Y$ on the final part with $UX,UY\le1/2$. Then $XY\le1$. Also $UB\ge100$ and $BZ\le1/2$, so $XZ\ge99$ and $YZ\ge99$. The subpath from $X$ to $Y$ passes through $Z$ and has length at least $XZ+ZY\ge198$.
